verdict.rationale: FireHydrant documents Runbooks as its automation engine. They evaluate conditions whenever an incident is declared and then run steps unattended, such as creating Slack channels, sending webhooks, and posting AI summaries. Alert rules also turn events into alerts and route them without human action. All of this automation is event-triggered within incident workflows only, so the story's broader 'autonomous background' scope is only partly evidenced. Missing for 10: time-based or recurring scheduled automations independent of incidents, autonomous AI-agent actions beyond summaries and suggestions, and independent or hands-on corroboration that runbooks run reliably unattended.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Runbooks are FireHydrant's automation engine. They define and automate a workflow of steps and actions according to specified conditions.
Any time an incident is declared, Runbooks evaluate their conditions to decide whether or not they should trigger.
Automate manual tasks such as creating incident Slack channels, Jira tickets, meeting bridges, and more
If you have internal systems that perform tasks like rolling back deployments, you may want to dispatch an HTTP request from FireHydrant to those systems.
when a Rule matches, the Event is turned into an Alert and routed to the relevant party
